name: Ferrari 348 TB
description:
### Ferrari 348 TB

* Rosso Corsa over Tan 
* Full matching numbers 
* Odometer: 36,673 Miles 
* Authorized dealer car 

The Ferrari 348 TB stands as one of the final truly raw expressions in Maranello’s V8 lineage — the last V8 sign-off by Enzo Ferrari and the last of the dog-leg gated shifter. All amazing traits before refinement began to take center stage in her younger sister, F355.

Retaining the mechanical spirit and intimacy of the earlier Ferraris, the 348 introduced a new level of performance and design language that unmistakably echoed the icon of the 1980s — the Testarossa.

Enhanced by a monocoque chassis and Ferrari’s Formula 1-inspired longitudinal flat-plane V8, paired with a transverse gearbox — the very architecture that gave the model her TB (Trasversale Berlinetta) designation and her unmistakable roar — the 348 marked the beginning of a new technical chapter for Maranello’s mid-engined V8 cars.

The Tipo F119, with her sharper wedge profile, signature ’80s side strakes, and wider stance signaled the arrival of a more modern supercar identity, while never abandoning the rawness that defined Ferrari’s golden analog era. 

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents**  
**Ferrari 348 TB — The Rebellion**  
*From our Analog Ferrari Collection*

name: Ferrari F355 Berlinetta
description:
### Ferrari F355 Berlinetta

* **Gated Manual**
* Rosso Corsa over Nero
* Factory carbon fiber bucket seats — believed to have been specified on fewer than 4% of total F355 production
* Period-correct BBS Iding Power 19” wheels
* Desirable early three-spoke non-airbag steering wheel
* Early Bosch Motronic 2.7, OBDI car with sharper throttle response and a more aggressive exhaust note
* Odometer: 38,483 kilometers
* Authorized dealer car

The F355 Berlinetta remains one of Maranello’s purest expressions of the analog era — a car defined by the perfect balance between purity and practicality.

Equipped with one of the most tactile open-gate manual transmissions ever fitted to a road car, along with a flat-plane V8 that screams a high pitch F1-style exhaust note to her redline at 8500 rpm.

What makes this particular example truly special is her specification — unquestionably one of the highest-specced F355s in Thailand, and in the World.

**Gated manual.**
**Carbon bucket seats.**
**Motronic 2.7.**
**Three-spoke steering wheel.**

Every box ticked — exactly as Ferrari collectors would want.

The perfectly specced car from the perfect analog model.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents**
**Ferrari F355 Berlinetta — The Perfection**
*From our Analog Ferrari Collection*

name: BMW M3 CS
description:
### BMW M3 CS

* **Manual**
* Odometer: 9,799 miles
* Interlagos Blue (A30), an exclusive paint option for the CS
* Cinnamon interior
* 1 of 275 RHD M3 CS manufactured, rarer than the M3 CSL
* Factory-equipped with the “ZCP” Competition Package, derived from the M3 CSL

Some say the only thing that stopped the M3 CSL from being the perfect car was the fact that it was offered only with SMG II, not a manual transmission.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents the BMW M3 CS — carryi**ng major features from the CSL, and a bit more: 13.7” cross-drilled brake rotors, a sharper 14.5:1 steering rack, M Track Mode for DSC, and 19” CSL wheels.

Most importantly, however, is the Getrag Type D S6S420G. For the lucky few who have had the privilege of shifting through the gears of the S6S420G, it is often described as cutting a hot knife through butter — engaging and highly satisfying. Almost as if the gearbox draws your hand in, welcoming and hungry for the next shift.

Tastefully optioned from the factory in Interlagos Blue — exclusive to the M3 CS — over a beautiful Cinnamon interior. A combination that even the talent of our photographers cannot fully capture, and must truly be seen in the flesh.

name: Honda NSX-R
description:
### Honda NSX-R

* **NA1 Model**
* Championship White
* 1 of 483 Manufactured, Car #30
* Odometer: 31,395 Kilometers

Created in 1992 as Honda’s purest expression of performance from the NSX platform, the NA1 NSX-R underwent a meticulous factory weight-reduction program: sound deadening removed, thinner glass, lightweight components, titanium shift knob, Recaro carbon-kevlar seats, and a hand-balanced version of Honda’s legendary C30A VTEC V6.

Power remained officially unchanged at 280 HP — but that was never the point. Perfection was never about power.

Only 483 examples of the NA1 NSX-R were ever produced, placing her in the same rarity league as the Ferrari Enzo (40X) and BMW M1 (453). The 4XX Club.

Our example is finished in Championship White — Honda’s historic motorsport color first earned through its inaugural Formula One victory. The NSX-R remains not merely a Japanese classic, but one of the most important — perhaps the most important — analog performance cars ever created by Japan.

The NSX-R became the machine that quietly forced the world’s greatest manufacturers to rethink how a driver’s car should feel. Italy, Germany, and the United Kingdom suddenly found themselves relearning what they had spent decades mastering.

The rulebook was rewritten by Japan.

**The Sweet Payback**

name: Alfa Romeo Alfasud Sprint
description:
### Alfa Romeo Alfasud Sprint

* **Series 1**
* Finished in White
* Boxer Engine and Sunroof Configuration
* Odometer: 96,809 Kilometers
* 1 of Only 2 Examples known by us in Thailand

Created during the 1970s — an era where Europe was still obsessed with lightweight engineering and mechanical intimacy — the Alfa Romeo Alfasud Sprint arrived as Alfa Romeo’s radical answer to what an affordable sporting coupé could become.

Beneath the delicate Giugiaro-designed hatchback-styled body sat one of the most advanced layouts ever engineered into an entry-level coupé of her era: front-wheel drive paired with Alfa Romeo’s low-mounted flat-four boxer engine.

The boxer configuration allowed the engine to sit impossibly low in the chassis, lowering the center of gravity and giving the Sprint a character few cars of its class could replicate. The steering felt alive. The nose reacted instantly. The car rotated with an eagerness that reminded the world that lightweight engineering was still an art form in Italy.

Today, surviving Alfasud Sprints remain extraordinarily scarce worldwide, with only two examples currently known by us in Thailand.

One of the rarest Alfa Romeo models in Thailand.

name: Toyota Celica 1600 GTV
description:
### Toyota Celica 1600 GTV

* **Japanese Domestic Market “Flat Nose” TA22 Model**
* Coral Red
* 1600cc 2T-G DOHC Twin-Cam Engine
* Weber 50 DCO Carburetors with Hayashi Racing Headers
* Engine and Full Panel Restored in 2018

By 1974, Japan had stopped trying to imitate Europe.

It had begun competing with it.

The Toyota Celica 1600 GTV represented the very best of Toyota’s emerging performance philosophy during the golden age of Japanese motoring — lightweight, reliable, mechanically honest, and engineered to deliver maximum enjoyment from modest displacement.

At her heart sits Toyota’s 2T-G twin-cam engine, developed with Yamaha and inspired by the same engineering ambition that would later define some of Japan’s most celebrated performance cars. Fed by Weber 50 DCO carburetors and breathing through Hayashi Racing headers, the soundtrack is every bit as important as the numbers.

Our example was restored in 2018 by Vintage JDM specialist and thoughtfully upgraded with period-correct performance modifications but remains faithful to the spirit of Japanese tuning culture that emerged during the 1970s.

name: Bentley Brooklands
description:
### Bentley Brooklands

* **AAS Authorised Dealer Car**
* Navy Blue with Red Coachline
* Cream Connolly Leather with Navy Piping
* 6.75-Litre Rolls-Royce V8
* Hand-Built in Crewe

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents a la**nd yacht from the United Kingdom — the Bentley Brooklands.

She was conceived not as a sports car, but as a gentleman’s express: a motorcar designed to cross continents in near silence while carrying the unmistakable presence of Crewe’s finest. Retailing at approximately £82,000 in 1992, the Brooklands occupied a very different league of luxury — at a time when a new Porsche 964 Carrera could be purchased for around £48,000.

Our example is finished in deep Navy Blue with a hand-painted red coachline, over a Cream Connolly leather interior accented by matching Navy piping.
Together, the specification captures the understated elegance that defined Bentley during the final years of its traditional coachbuilt era.

For us, the Brooklands serves as a reminder of an era when luxury was measured not by screens, gadgets or software, but by Connolly leather, polished walnut, and the quiet confidence of a five-foot bonnet leading the way.

name: Lamborghini Diablo VT
description:
### Lamborghini Diablo VT

* **VT (Viscous Traction) All-Wheel Drive**
* Giallo Orion over Nero with Giallo Piping
* Only 6,252 Kilometers from New
* Early Pop-Up Headlight, Low Dash Model
* Full Chassis & Paint Restoration
* Mechanical Service by Renazzo Motor

The Diablo VT was Lamborghini’s answer to a simple problem: how to harness the fury of a naturally aspirated V12 without taming her character. Through its innovative Viscous Traction system, up to 25% of torque could be transferred to the front wheels when required, creating the blueprint that would later define every flagship V12 Lamborghini from the Murciélago and Aventador to today’s Revuelto.

Beneath the engine cover sits a 5.7-litre, 48-valve V12 descended directly from the original masterpiece conceived by Giotto Bizzarrini in 1963. No turbochargers. No traction control. No ABS. Just twelve cylinders, 485 horsepower, and outrageous 335 mm-wide rear tyres.

The name Diablo translates to “Devil” in Spanish. A fitting title for a machine that rewards courage and demands absolute respect from her driver.

A car built for brave men willing to tame her.

Since the founding of GENERATIONAL, many extraordinary automobiles have passed through our showroom. Few possess the theatre, presence, and sheer intimidation factor of the Diablo VT.

Our example has undergone a comprehensive body and paint restoration by one of Thailand’s leading restoration specialists, while all mechanical works have been entrusted to Renazzo Motor, Thailand’s official Lamborghini authorised dealer. No detail has been overlooked.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents the Lamborghi**ni Diablo VT.

From The Natee Masathienvong Collection.

name: Ferrari 512 TR
description:
### Ferrari 512 TR

* **1 of only 88 RHD ever produced**
* Authorized Dealer
* Rosso Corsa over Tan
* Odometer displays 6,166 kilometres following a factory instrument replacement; documented original mileage ~ 38,000 kilometres

The Testarossa changed everything about Ferrari‘s 12 cylinders flagship.

Introduced in 1984, the F110 platform represented Ferrari’s complete departure from the traditional front-engined V12 flagship. Its dramatic “cheese grater” side strakes, impossibly wide rear track and flat-twelve engine created an entirely new identity for the marque. The Testarossa became a cultural phenomenon. Immortalised by Miami Vice, celebrated by celebrities and entrepreneurs, it became the definitive symbol of the excess, ambition and optimism that characterised America’s economic boom of the 1980s.

The 512 TR arrived in 1991 as a comprehensive evolution rather than a simple facelift. The flat-twelve was repositioned lower within the chassis, improving the centre of gravity and significantly enhancing handling characteristics. Aerodynamic revisions reduced lift and increased stability at speed, while the interior was redesigned to provide greater comfort and usability without sacrificing the drama that defined the model.

Since acquiring the car, Khun Natee has driven it regularly over the past 10 years, covering 6,166 kilometres to ensure the car remained active and properly exercised. During his stewardship, the car has benefited from extensive mechanical and cosmetic attention. A NOS steering rack, as well as the main shaft, layshaft and synchromesh components. The engine has also undergone a comprehensive refresh to ensure the car performs as intended when the car was new.

The bodywork has been thoroughly restored and remains free from corrosion in the areas commonly prone to rust on the model, including the door sills, floors and pillars. Together with the extensively refreshed suspension and paintwork, the result is an exceptionally well-presented example of Ferrari’s celebrated flat-twelve GT.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents The Ferrari 512 TR.**

From The Natee Masathienvong Collection.

name: Porsche 911 Turbo
description:
### Porsche 911 Turbo

* **993 Turbo S in all but name — and a little more**
* Specified through Porsche’s highest level of personalization, the “Sonderwunsch” (Special Wishes) programme
* Factory X50 WLS II package, increasing output to 450 horsepower — matching the Turbo S
* Equipped with the corresponding Turbo S air intakes, rear wing and front bumper
* Ocean Blue Metallic over Tan Leather with bespoke Walnut interior
* A genuine one-off specification

The Porsche 993 Turbo occupies a unique position in the history of the 911. She was the first turbocharged 911 to feature twin turbochargers and all-wheel drive, combining supercar performance with everyday usability in a way no previous Turbo had achieved.

Yet for a select group of customers, even the standard Turbo was not enough.

Today, personalization has become the cornerstone of the supercar industry. Programmes such as McLaren Special Operations (MSO), Ferrari Tailor Made and Lamborghini Ad Personam allow customers to commission vehicles tailored to their individual tastes, transforming exclusivity into a key selling point.

But this car was doing exactly that nearly three decades earlier.

Long benevolence bespoke commissions became a marketing strategy, Porsche’s Sonderwunsch programme quietly offered a select group of VIP clients the opportunity to work directly with the factory to create truly individual motorcars. In many ways, it was the blueprint for the personalization programmes that define the modern supercar market today.

Finished in Ocean Blue Metallic over Tan Leather with a bespoke Walnut interior, she embodies a period when Porsche would build almost anything a VIP customer desired, provided they were willing to ask.

A Turbo S in all but name, and more.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents The Porsche 911 Turbo.**

From The Natee Masathienvong Collection.

name: Porsche 911 SuperSport Cabriolet
description:
### Porsche 911 SuperSport Cabriolet

* **Factory M491 “Works Turbo Look” specification**
* Features the Turbo’s distinctive fender flares, front spoiler and Tea Tray rear wing
* Factory fitted with the 930 Turbo’s uprated suspension, braking system and Fuchs alloy wheels
* Silver Metallic over Red Interior
* Odometer reads 39,267 miles

Few shapes in automotive history are as iconic as the Porsche 930 Turbo. The sexy rear arches. The Tea Tray rear wing. Two unmistakable design elements that came to define the excess and optimism of the 1980s. It was the poster car of a generation.

It was also one of the most intimidating road cars ever built.

The combination of a rear-mounted engine, short wheelbase and explosive turbocharged power delivery earned the 930 its infamous “Widowmaker” reputation. When the boost arrived, it arrived all at once.

For those who desired the look without the risk, Porsche introduced option code M491, better known as the “SuperSport”.

Delivering all the visual drama of the Turbo while retaining the balance, predictability and usability of the naturally aspirated Carrera, the M491 was far more than a cosmetic package. It received the Turbo’s wider bodywork, uprated brakes, suspension and Fuchs wheels, combined with Porsche’s proven 3.2-litre flat-six, G50 transmission, open-top cabriolet, to create one of the most complete air-cooled cabriolet 911.

Everything people loved about the 930 Turbo, without the thing they fear.

Finished in timeless Silver Metallic over Red Leather, our example represents one of the most elegant interpretations of Porsche’s celebrated Turbo Look formula.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents The Porsche 911 SuperSport Cabriolet.**

From The Natee Masathienvong Collection.

name: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS
description:
### Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS

* **The pinnacle of the 718 model range**
* Powered by the 4.0-litre naturally aspirated flat-six directly from the 992 GT3
* Configured with motorsport-focused options, including steel brakes similar to GT3R and GT3 RSR
* AAS Authorised Dealer Car
* White over Black with Blue inserts and matching Indigo Blue wheels
* Odometer: 3,882 kilometres

The Porsche RS badge has never been more desirable.

However, in our humble opinion, RS models have become increasingly expressive. Contrasting colours, exposed carbon, oversized decals and bold accent packages have transformed many modern RS into rolling statements. They are spectacular machines, but increasingly, they are also statements of one’s taste.

Many seasoned Porsche enthusiasts have begun gravitating back towards subtler specifications. GT3 Touring rather than GT3 RS. Specification that whisper rather than shout. Cars that prioritise purpose over presence.

This GT4 RS is exactly that.

Finished in White, her specification is restrained yet deeply considered. Indigo Blue wheels are echoed by matching blue seatbelts, roll cage and interior details, creating a cohesive motorsport-inspired theme rather than a collection of contrasting options.

More importantly, she was configured by a Motorsport-focused mind.

Instead of Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes, she is equipped with steel brakes—the choice favoured by many experienced track drivers and endurance racing teams, including Porsche Works Race cars as seen in GT3 R and GT3 RSR programmes, for their consistency, serviceability and ease of replacement under sustained circuit use.

GENERATIONAL proudly presents

 The Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS.

name: Nissan Skyline GT-R
description:
### Nissan Skyline GT-R

* Full panel restoration to factory-original condition by specialist SY Unique, followed by a bare-metal respray by SY Antique, with complete documentation throughout the restoration
* Restored using only original Nissan OEM parts
* Stock RB26DETT engine overhauled by GT-R specialist Toon Engine Shop
* Black Pearl Metallic (732)
* Odometer: 26,033 Kilometers
* Stored in a 24-hour climate-controlled garage
* 1994 model year, the final year of R32 GT-R production

Introduced in 1989, the Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) was developed as Japan's answer to the world's finest performance cars. Powered by the legendary RB26DETT, backed by the ATTESA E-TS and Super-HICAS, she became the machine that Australia's Wheels magazine would famously nickname “Godzilla.”

Godzilla's dominance was immediate, destroying everything in its path. The R32 claimed 29 “consecutive” victories in the JTCC, won the 1990, 1991 and 1992 Spa 24 Hours, conquered the Australian Touring Car Championship in both 1991 and 1992, and famously defeated Australia's V8s to win the 1991 and 1992 Bathurst 1000 on their home soil. The monster from Japan had crossed the ocean to conquer the world. No one could escape the R32, and to this day, the R32 GT-R remains the most successful racing GT-R ever built.

Our example has undergone a meticulous, factory-correct restoration by two of Thailand's leading specialists, SY Unique & SY Antique, with its original RB26DETT professionally overhauled by Toon Engine Shop. Every stage of the restoration was documented, with the complete history accompanying the car.

Finding a stock R32 GT-R that remains faithful to its original factory specification in concours condition is becoming increasingly difficult, not just in Thailand but the world.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents**
**Nissan Skyline GT-R**

name: Porsche 911 Carrera S
description:
### Porsche 911 Carrera S

* Arena Red Metallic
* Factory wide-body Carrera S (Type-993)
* 3.6-litre NA VarioRam
* Tiptronic S transmission
* Comprehensive service history with AAS
* Odometer: 124,641 kilometres

Introduced in 1995, the Porsche 911 Carrera S (Type-993) marked the final chapter of an era that had begun more than three decades earlier. It belonged to the last generation of NA, air-cooled 911s before Porsche embraced water cooling — and, decades later, turbocharging across the Carrera range.

Borrowing the unmistakable wide body of the 993 Turbo, yet remaining faithful to rear-wheel drive and naturally aspirated simplicity, the Carrera S has long been regarded as one of the purest expressions of the 993. Less about outright speed, more about proportion, balance, and the unmistakable character that only an air-cooled flat-six can deliver.

And yet, among air-cooled Porsches, the 993 feels remarkably modern. Enthusiasts often consider the evolutionary leap from the 964 to the 993 greater than that from the 993 to the 996, particularly in refinement and usability.

Our example is presented in Arena Red Metallic, one of the defining colours of the 993 generation. Under different light, she shifts from deep burgundy to rich crimson, giving the wide-body silhouette a presence that is elegant rather than loud. She has been maintained to an exceptional standard, supported by a comprehensive service history with AAS.

The updated VarioRam engine brings stronger low-end torque and greater flexibility for traffic use, while the Tiptronic S makes the car effortless to enjoy every day — and accessible to every driver in the family.

She is a remarkably well-rounded Porsche: special enough for Cars & Coffee among other 911s, fast enough to keep company with modern water-cooled Porsches on a road trip, yet civilised enough to be enjoyed every day.

For those searching for one Porsche to do almost everything, perhaps this is it.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents the Porsche 911 Carrera S.**

name: Mercedes-Benz 300a “Adenauer”
description:
### Mercedes-Benz 300a “Adenauer”

Introduced in 1951, the Mercedes-Benz 300 represented the return of Stuttgart to the very top of the luxury automobile world. It was the largest and fastest series-production car built in Germany at the time, and Mercedes-Benz regarded it as the successor to its pre-war “Grand Mercedes.”

The 300 soon became the automobile of choice for heads of state, industrialists and some of the most influential figures of post-war Europe. Yet no individual would become more closely associated with it than Konrad Adenauer, the first Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany.

Adenauer’s preference for the 300 was absolute. He reportedly insisted that he would only be driven only in a Mercedes-Benz 300 — even during official trips abroad. Over the course of his chancellorship and afterward, he used six different examples, creating an association so enduring that the W186 and W189 generations simply became known as the “Adenauer.”

Long before the S-Class existed, this was Mercedes-Benz at its highest level.

Finished in an elegant two-tone combination, our 300a represents more than the flagship Mercedes of the 1950s. It belongs to a generation of automobiles that accompanied a country through its reconstruction and returned the three-pointed star to the world stage.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents Mercedes-Be**nz 300a “Adenauer”

name: Austin Mini Mk1 Cooper S
description:
### Austin Mini Mk1 Cooper S

* Vintage Car Club of Thailand Concours 2025 — First Prize, “Mini Cars” Class
* Imported new to Thailand — Chassis No. AA2S7-
* Engine & gearbox fully overhauled
* Fully restored body shell
* Newton Commercial UK interior
* Odometer: 68,263 kilometres

Introduced in 1959 and designed by Sir Alec Issigonis, the original Mini revolutionised the small car with its transverse-engine, front-wheel-drive layout.

John Cooper soon recognised its sporting potential, leading to the Mini Cooper in 1961 and the more powerful Cooper S in 1963. Light, agile and remarkably capable, the Cooper S became one of the defining performance cars of its era, made world-famous by outright victories at the Monte Carlo Rally in 1964, 1965 and 1967.

Our Mk1 Cooper S has been comprehensively restored using only NOS and period-correct components sourced from the UK. The level of her restoration was recognised by the Vintage Car Club of Thailand, where she was awarded First Prize in the “Mini Cars” class at the 2025 Concours. Apart from the cosmetic perfection, she was tried and tested in Bangkok’s traffic and proven very robust and reliable.

Our Mk1 marks the beginning of the Cooper S story — and an important chapter in our “The 41 Years of Mini Collection.”

name: Rover Mini Cooper
description:
### Rover Mini Cooper

* Originally imported to Thailand by Thai Ultimate Car
* Original Thai registration since new
* 1,275 c.c. SPI fuel-injected engine
* 4-speed manual transmission
* British Racing Green
* Genuine and original 12” alloy wheels, Rover’s A/C and interior
* Original etched chassis number retained on all glass

By the 1990s, the Mini had evolved considerably from the revolutionary little car introduced by Sir Alec Issigonis in 1959, yet its unmistakable character remained largely unchanged.

The Rover Mini Cooper represented a more modern chapter of the Cooper story. Its classic proportions and compact dimensions were now paired with a 1,275 c.c. single-point fuel-injected engine, bringing greater refinement and everyday usability while retaining the simplicity and charm that had defined the Mini for decades.

Our 1993 Cooper is finished in an iconic British Racing Green and was originally supplied to Thailand by Thai Ultimate Car (TUC) new. Remarkably well preserved, she retains her original interior, genuine Rover air conditioning and factory glass, with the chassis number still etched into every pane — details that speak to the originality of the car.

A wonderfully preserved example from the later years of classic Mini production, and another important chapter in our “The 41 Years of Mini Collection.”

name: Rover Mini Cooper BSCC — Mark VI
description:
### Rover Mini Cooper BSCC — Mark VI

* Built to celebrate the 30th Anniversary of the Mini’s British Saloon Car Championship triumph in 1964
* One of only 750 BSCC Minis produced
* Brooklands Green
* 1,275 c.c. fuel-injected engine

By the mid-1990s, the classic Mini had already established itself as one of the world’s great racing icons. Its extraordinary competition history had transformed what began as an ingenious small car into a genuine giant-killer — a legacy Rover celebrated with the Mini Cooper BSCC.

Introduced in 1994, the BSCC — British Saloon Car Championship — was a limited edition based on the Mark VI Mini Cooper. Just 750 examples were produced to commemorate the 30th anniversary of the Mini’s triumph in the 1964 British Saloon Car Championship, when Warwick Banks took the championship driving a Mini Cooper S.

Finished in Brooklands Green, the BSCC embraced a particularly traditional British specification, while its 1,275 c.c. fuel-injected engine retained the lively character synonymous with the Cooper name.

Our BSCC represents an interesting point in the Mini’s evolution: modern enough to benefit from fuel injection and the refinements of the Mark VI generation, yet still unmistakably connected to the simplicity, proportions and driving character of the original.

A celebration of the Mini Cooper’s British sporting heritage, produced in just 750 examples — and another important chapter in our “The 41 Years of Mini Collection.”

name: Rover Mini Paul Smith
description:
### Rover Mini Paul Smith

* One of only 1,800 Paul Smith Minis produced worldwide
* Paul Smith Blue
* 1,275 c.c. fuel-injected engine
* Automatic transmission
* Signature Citrus Green detailing
* Paul Smith special-edition badging

By the late 1990s, the classic Mini was approaching the end of its remarkable four-decade production journey. To celebrate one of Britain’s greatest automotive icons, Rover collaborated with another great name in British design — Paul Smith. One of the most fitting collaborations in automotive history; a match made in heaven — or, perhaps, Nottingham.

Limited to just 1,800 cars worldwide, the Paul Smith Mini, using the Mk VII as its base, combined the timeless shape of the original Mini with Sir Paul Smith’s unmistakable eye for colour and detail.

Even the famous Paul Smith Blue has a story. During the design process, Rover engineers asked Sir Paul which shade of blue he wanted. His answer was the blue shirt he happened to be wearing that day — he simply cut a piece from its hem and handed the fabric to them to colour-match the paint. Yeah, it’s that cool.

Beyond the exterior, the Paul Smith Mini is defined by its playful hidden details. A green Great Britain island motif sits within the front grille, 24-carat gold PS badge, while inside, a Citrus Green glovebox contrasts against the black leather. Look closer and the theme continues throughout the car — right down to details as small as the green coil wiring and radiator fan. It is Sir Paul’s attention to the smallest details that brings his philosophy of “classic with a twist” to life throughout the Mini.

Our Paul Smith is finished in that very signature blue inspired by Sir Paul’s shirt, paired with a 1,275 c.c. fuel-injected engine and automatic transmission. Its understated blue exterior contrasts with unexpected flashes of Citrus Green hidden throughout the car — a typically Paul Smith touch.

Two British design icons brought together in one very special Mini, and another important chapter in our “The 41 Years of Mini Collection.”

name: Rover Mini Cooper Sport 500
description:
### Rover Mini Cooper Sport 500

* One of the final 500 classic Minis ever produced
* British Racing Green
* 1,275 c.c. MPI fuel-injected engine
* 4-speed manual transmission
* 13” Minilite-style alloy wheels
* Original Thai registration from new
* Odometer: 1,000 kilometres
* Believed to be one of the lowest-mileage Mini Cooper Sport 500s in the world

Every great story deserves a proper ending.

After 41 years of continuous production, the classic Mini was approaching the end of the road in 2000. To mark the final chapter of one of the most important cars in automotive history, Rover created the Mini Cooper Sport 500 — the final 500 classic Minis built for the UK market.

Based on the final Mk VII evolution, the Sport 500 represented the classic Mini at its most developed. Its familiar shape remained unmistakably connected to Issigonis’ original 1959 design, but underneath sat the later 1,275 c.c. MPI fuel-injected engine, paired here with a 4-speed manual transmission and wider 13” Minilite-style alloy wheels.

Our Sport 500 is finished in quintessential British Racing Green and has travelled an extraordinary 1,000 kilometres from new. She is believed to be one of the lowest-mileage Sport 500s in existence — an exceptionally preserved example of the Mini’s final chapter.

From the first Mk1 to one of the final 500.

The perfect bookend to “The 41 Years of Mini Collection” — five Minis telling the story from the beginning of classic Mini production in 1959 to its final farewell in 2000.

41 years. Five Minis. Small cars, big history.

name: Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG Coupé Black Series
description:
### Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG Coupé Black Series

* 1 of ~800 produced worldwide and ~135 in RHD
* 1 of only 2 in Thailand
* Diamond White
* 6.2-litre naturally aspirated M156 V8
* 517 horsepower

AMG had represented the pinnacle of Mercedes-Benz performance for decades.

Then came Black Series.

Introduced in 2006, Black Series took the AMG formula further — more power, less weight, wider bodywork, bigger aero and a sharper chassis.

The C63 AMG Coupé Black Series became one of its greatest expressions. At its heart sits AMG's legendary 6.2-litre NA M156 V8, producing 517 horsepower, surrounded by dramatically widened bodywork, carbon-fibre front canards and rear wing, with its chassis, cooling and suspension all improved from the standard C63 AMG with the circuit firmly in mind.

Our example is finished in Diamond White and is one of approximately 800 produced worldwide, with around 135 built in RHD. Only two are known to reside in Thailand.

She represents the C-Class at perhaps her most outrageous — and, importantly, the final C-Class Black Series powered by a large-displacement, naturally aspirated V8 before the era of smaller turbocharged engines took over. And for us, the M156 delivers one of the greatest engine sounds ever to come from a Mercedes-Benz.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents**
**Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG Coupé Black Series**

Offered exclusively through GENERATIONAL.

name: BMW M3 CSL
description:
### BMW M3 CSL

* 1 of 422 UK-delivered examples
* Black Sapphire Metallic
* 3.2-litre NA S54 straight-six
* 360 horsepower
* Carbon-fibre roof & body components
* Pristine condition

There was a time when BMW M meant one thing above all else — motorsport.

BMW M took the E46 M3 and stripped away everything that wasn't necessary. Less weight. More power. More carbon fibre. More focus.

The result was the M3 CSL — Coupé Sport Leichtbau.

The pinnacle of the E46 — or, should we dare say, the pinnacle of modern-era BMW.

Just 422 examples were delivered to the UK, making the CSL one of the rarest and most significant M cars of its generation.

At her heart sits BMW's legendary 3.2-litre naturally aspirated S54 straight-six, producing 360 horsepower and revving to 7,900 rpm. The CSL went further with a carbon-fibre roof, lightweight body panels, carbon airbox, lightweight interior and a chassis developed with the Nürburgring firmly in mind.

Our CSL is finished in Black Sapphire Metallic and presented in pristine condition. We believe she is one of the finest-condition E46s in Thailand, alongside the low-mileage M3 CS Manual also in our collection.

It is our honour to represent two of Thailand's M3 CSLs, one in each of the two colours offered from the factory.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents**
**BMW M3 CSL**

name: Porsche 911 GT2
description:
### Porsche 911 GT2

* Polar Silver Metallic over Black
* 1 of 16 UK RHD Mk.II
* ~27,000 miles
* Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes
* Never tracked and never raced
* Exceptionally well preserved

Introduced in 2001, the 996 GT2 was Porsche’s ultimate road-going 911 of its generation — the very top of the 996 lineup.

Derived from the 996 Turbo, but developed with a very different purpose, the GT2 abandoned all-wheel drive in favour of rear-wheel drive, shed weight, gained more power, and was engineered with one objective in mind: maximum performance with minimum interference between the driver and the car.

The 996 GT2 is the best of both worlds — the agility and lightness of the 996 GT3 combined with the absolute turbocharged force of the 996 Turbo.

In the end of her production in 2004, Porsche release the GT2 Mark II, with bigger twin-turbo, improved ECU, dampers and ABS system, power jump from 462 to 483 horsepowers, making the GT2 Mk.II the most powerful street-legal 996 ever produced. With a 6-Speed Manual, Rear-wheel drive, No stability control, No traction control and No electronic safety net.

Stuttgart designed the GT2 for brave drivers. And within the Porsche community, GT2 owners have long been regarded among the most hardcore — and perhaps bravest and craziest — of the breed.

In the long table of Porsche owners, the head of the table is always reserved for GT2 drivers.

But perhaps the most remarkable thing about our 996 GT2 is not how fast she can go, but how little she has been asked to.

We once connected to the car through her OBDII port and studied her engine rev history. Across roughly 27,000 miles of her entire life, the total time spent at redline was approximately three seconds.

Three seconds.

She remains remarkably original and exceptionally well preserved — a rare example of the 996 GT2 that has lived her life more as a collector’s car than a track weapon.

Almost as if she was reserved for the next owner to decide what comes next.

Tracked. Raced. Or simply kept as the centrepiece of a serious Porsche collection.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents Porsche 911 GT2**

name: Porsche 911 GT3 RS
description:
### Porsche 911 GT3 RS

* Carrera White with Blue decals and wheels
* Service at AAS
* 1 of only 140 RHD worldwide
* 1 of 682 produced worldwide
* Rarest and lightest GT3 RS variant ever

In 2003, Porsche started the modern GT3 RS phenomenon — the foundation upon which every GT3 RS that followed was built.

Based on the 996 GT3, Porsche Motorsport went further. Less weight. More downforce. A polycarbonate rear window. Carbon-fibre bodywork. Adjustable suspension. A fixed rear wing. And the legendary 3.6-litre naturally aspirated Mezger flat-six producing 381 horsepower, with a dry weight of approximately 1,360 kg — making her the lightest and rawest of the GT3 RS generation.

Only available from Stuttgart in Carrera White with Blue or Red graphics and wheels. A tribute to the legendary 2.7 Carrera RS.

Porsche never officially sold the 996 GT3 RS in the United States, and for years, that kept the 996 GT3 RS largely outside the world’s largest Porsche collecting market. As these cars reach their 25-year eligibility under U.S. import rules, the doors to that market begin to open.

The first 2003 examples become eligible in 2028, just a little over a year from now, we believe the market will change dramatically for the model.

The 996 GT3 RS has already begun to show where she can go. A 2004 example reached $500,000 at auction in March 2026.

We believe that once the 25-year clock fully opens the U.S. market, the 996 GT3 RS could rocket toward $800,000, or even become the first million-dollar street-legal 996. Just like the 993 GT2 before her. Mark our words.

Our example is finished in Carrera White with Blue RS graphics and matching Blue wheels, presenting in low-mileage and exceptionally well-preserved condition, with servicing carried out by AAS throughout her life. She is now waiting for her new visionary owner. Whether the intention is collecting, spirited driving, or track days, she has all the original formula of what makes Porsche enthusiasts love the RS.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents Porsche 911 GT3 RS.**

name: Nismo R32 GT-R Clubman Race Spec - Tribute
description:
### Nismo R32 GT-R Clubman Race Spec - Tribute

* Based on a Thai BNR32
* Tribute to the original Nismo Clubman Race Spec
* Over THB 4 million invested in original, aftermarket and restoration parts

Nismo’s Omori Factory is the epicenter of Nissan’s most serious performance development. Beyond supplying individual Nismo components, Omori offered complete conversion programmes for owners who wanted to take their Skyline GT-R further, with the Clubman Race Spec (CRS) representing one of the most significant interpretations of the R32 GT-R. The philosophy was not simply to modify the car, but to develop it as a complete system, with engine, drivetrain, suspension, brakes, wheels, exhaust, bodywork and interior working together as one cohesive package, bringing Nismo’s motorsport knowledge closer to the road.

The original CRS became one of the defining expressions of the R32 GT-R tuning era, combining Nismo’s engineering expertise with the Japanese aftermarket culture that surrounded the Skyline. Rather than focusing on individual upgrades, the objective was to create a more focused and cohesive GT-R, with every component contributing to the balance, response and character of the complete car.

Our car is a tribute to that philosophy, based on a Thai BNR32 and finished in Gun Grey Metallic. The project was entrusted to Sky Gallery, one of Thailand’s leading GT-R specialists, with the objective of creating a complete R32 GT-R rather than simply assembling a collection of performance upgrades. More than THB 4 million has been invested, combining original Nismo and Nissan OEM components, carefully selected aftermarket parts and extensive restoration work.

The result is our interpretation of the R32 GT-R Clubman Race Spec — a complete car built around the principles of the original Omori programme, where restoration, performance and design are considered together rather than as separate modifications. It is not presented as an original Nismo CRS, but as a carefully constructed tribute to one of the most influential complete-car philosophies of the Japanese GT-R era.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents Nismo R32 GT-R Clubma**n Race Spec - Tribute.

name: Nismo 400R - Tribute
description:
### Nismo 400R - Tribute

* Based on a Thai BCNR33
* Tribute build inspired by the original Nismo 400R
* Over 150 parts replaced or restored
* More than THB 5 million invested in the build

In 1996, the Nismo 400R was developed as a complete car, producing 400 horsepowers and combining Nismo’s racing experience with its knowledge of Japanese tuning culture. Originally planned for 100 cars, only 44 examples were ultimately produced, making it one of the rarest and most significant R33 GT-Rs ever created, occupying the same rarefied level as the R34 GT-R Z-Tune. Its value today reflects that rarity, with original examples achieving $857,500 at auction as recently as August 2026, following another 400R selling for $918,000 earlier this year.

In our opinion, among JDM cars, the 400R by Nismo is the equivalent of a Ferrari F40 LM by Michelotto.
The very top of the mountain.

Our car is a tribute build, based on a Thai BCNR33. The project was entrusted to Sky Gallery, Thailand’s leading GT-R specialist, with more than THB 5 million invested into the build. More than 150 individual parts have been replaced, restored or upgraded, combining original Nismo and Nissan OEM components, carefully selected aftermarket parts and extensive restoration work, with the objective of bringing the car back to an essentially like-new condition.

The result is our interpretation of the Nismo 400R — a complete-car tribute inspired by one of the most significant creations from Omori Factory.

**GENERATIONAL proudly presents Nismo 400R - Tribute.**
